strengths: Addresses critical gap in existing AFC benchmarks by providing first unified platform combining standalone implementation, full differentiability, 3D support, and multi-agent RL capabilities
Exceptionally comprehensive scope: 13 environments, 3 difficulty levels, 16k+ GPU hours of experiments with proper statistical reporting
Thorough technical validation: grid refinement studies, comparisons with prior work (Rabault et al. 2019, Wang et al. 2022b, Guastoni et al. 2023), multiple random seeds
Practical accessibility: single Python package, pip-installable, integrates seamlessly with Gymnasium, Stable-Baselines3, TorchRL; eliminates brittle CFD coupling
Valuable public resource: environments, datasets, trained models released; lowers barriers to entry for RL+flow control research
Thoughtful design: modular FluidEnv abstraction, unified action spaces, standardized train/val/test protocols enable reproducibility and transfer learning
Clear empirical findings: demonstrates SAC outperforms PPO; shows direct 2D→3D transfer and domain-size transfer work; enables future research
Honest treatment of limitations: acknowledges limited seeds for expensive tasks (3D cases), hyperparameter defaults, D-MPC proof-of-concept status
weaknesses: D-MPC evaluation incomplete: gradient-based control demonstrated only on CylinderJet2D-easy/medium/hard; main differentiability feature lacks systematic validation across environments and comparison with other differentiable methods (DPC, differentiable RL)
Limited random seeds for high-dimensional tasks: 3D Airfoil and CylinderJet3D evaluated with only 3 seeds due to computational constraints; undermines statistical robustness for these important cases

Hyperparameter exploration absent: only default SB3 hyperparameters used; acknowledged that this 'may not reflect optimal performance'; unexplained poor results (e.g., SAC with -4.7% drag on CylinderJet3D-hard) not investigated via tuning

Modest control improvements in several domains: CylinderJet3D-hard (2.4%), RBC3D (12-15%), TCF (12-20% vs 20% opposition baseline) raise questions about problem difficulty and value of learned control
Incomplete analysis of algorithm performance: limited discussion of why SAC outperforms PPO beyond 'convergence'; no investigation of failure modes or when/why methods break down
Scope limitations: incompressible Navier-Stokes only; no compressible flows, MHD, or multiphase systems; acknowledged as future work but narrows current impact
Computational accessibility: requires CUDA GPU; CPU-only execution not supported; limits adoption for resource-constrained researchers
Transfer learning results somewhat limited: 2D→3D and small→large domain transfer shown for specific cases (cylinder, TCF) but broader transferability claims unsubstantiated

strengths: Addresses genuine practical gap: eliminates fragile external CFD solver dependencies (OpenFOAM, FEniCS), providing unified PyTorch implementation
Comprehensive infrastructure: 13 diverse environments, multiple difficulty levels, standardized train/val/test protocol, multiple random seeds with confidence intervals, 16k GPU hours of experiments
Full end-to-end differentiability throughout benchmark enables gradient-based control methods, unlike existing benchmarks
Strong reproducibility commitment: all code, data, trained models, and hyperparameters publicly available
Rigorous experimental methodology with validation against prior work; clear presentation of limitations
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: primarily engineering integration of existing PICT solver with RL libraries; no novel algorithms or control theory

Incomplete validation of central claim (differentiability): D-MPC only demonstrated on one environment (CylinderJet2D) with insufficient baselines (10 seeds, 1 test episode); systematic comparisons with other gradient-based methods missing

Hyperparameter choices severely undermine claims: uses default SB3 hyperparameters acknowledged as suboptimal; makes algorithm comparisons unfair and violates RL evaluation best practices; confidence intervals frequently overlap making 'SAC reliably outperforms PPO' overstated

Limited research insights: experiments confirm known results (SAC > PPO on continuous control); no surprising findings; no investigation of what policies learn; no ablation studies; transfer learning shows sometimes-negative results without analysis

Narrow scope limits impact: incompressible flows only; simulation without real-world validation; RL-only comparison (no classical control baselines); only 10 test episodes per seed with high variance on hard tasks

Physical fidelity concerns: baseline discrepancies vs. prior work (3.84% error on cylinder drag); idealized domains without uncertainties or constraints; TCF results show RL underperforming opposition control at higher difficulties without explanation
CUDA requirement contradicts 'plug-and-play' framing: custom kernels prevent CPU execution; still introduces software dependencies despite claims of simplicity

Incomplete evaluation of key features: medium/hard 3D Airfoil omitted due to computational constraints; only 3-5 random seeds instead of recommended 10-20; computational barriers despite open-source release

Exceptional experimental rigor: 16,000 GPU hours, proper statistical methodology (95% bootstrap CIs, multiple seeds), standardized train/val/test protocol
Comprehensive technical validation showing agreement with prior work (cylinder drag 3.84% deviation, TCF results consistent with literature)
Elegant software design: FluidEnv abstraction seamlessly supports SARL, MARL, and gradient-based methods without modification
Outstanding reproducibility and community contribution: public release of code, trained models, datasets, and standardized evaluation protocols
Useful algorithmic insights (SAC superiority, MARL transfer learning properties) and transfer learning studies demonstrating domain-size generalization
Excellent presentation with clear architecture diagrams, comprehensive appendices, and outstanding flow field visualizations
weaknesses: Incomplete exploration of differentiability feature: only D-MPC proof-of-concept evaluated; no systematic comparison with other differentiable control methods despite this being core contribution
Limited statistical robustness: 5 random seeds for most environments, 3 for expensive 3D cases, which somewhat undermines reproducibility claims central to benchmark motivation
Hardware accessibility limitations: requires CUDA-enabled GPUs with custom kernels; CPU-only execution not supported, limiting adoption
Hyperparameter choices favoring consistency over optimality: default SB3 parameters may not represent best algorithm performance, acknowledged but unresolved
Incomplete 3D coverage: Airfoil 3D limited to easy difficulty only; medium/hard omitted due to computational cost
Limited analysis of problematic results: negative drag reductions in some runs (e.g., 3D CylinderJet hard SAC: -4.7%) not explained; no discussion of optimization difficulties
Modest scope: restricted to incompressible Navier-Stokes; does not extend to compressible flows, combustion, or multiphase systems

strengths: Addresses real fragmentation problem in AFC benchmarking with comprehensive solution; first benchmark simultaneously offering standalone implementation, full differentiability, MARL support, and 3D environments
Excellent experimental rigor: 25k GPU hours across 13 environments, 5 random seeds, standardized protocols, confidence intervals, and proper statistical reporting
Substantial public resource: all environments, trained models, initial domains released; eliminates external CFD dependencies and CFD expertise barriers
Well-designed system architecture: FluidEnv abstraction elegantly supports SARL, MARL, and gradient-based methods through unified interface
Proper numerical validation: cylinder drag within 3.84% of prior work; grid refinement study demonstrates RBC convergence; reproducibility details comprehensive
Transfer learning results interesting and show unexpected effectiveness of cross-dimensional (2D→3D) and cross-scale (small→large) transfer
weaknesses: Primarily engineering contribution combining existing components (PICT solver, standard RL algorithms, benchmark design practices) rather than novel methodology or algorithms
Algorithm comparisons compromised by default hyperparameters acknowledged as suboptimal; undermines stated motivation for benchmarking different methods systematically
Differentiability claims not fully validated: DPC evaluated on only 2 of 13 environments; training degradation on CylinderJet2D-easy-v0 unexplained (stopped at 10k vs 50k steps)
Modest practical improvements (7-8% drag reduction, 15-30% TCF, ~50% airfoil efficiency) with unclear real-world applicability given 25k GPU hour investment; no sim-to-real validation
Limited algorithmic insights: surprising findings (SAC>>PPO) lack mechanistic explanation; many results predictable from prior RL literature; no theoretical contributions

strengths: Well-executed systems integration combining PICT solver with PyTorch and standard RL interfaces, addressing real pain points in AFC-RL research fragmentation
Comprehensive and rigorous experimental methodology: 5 random seeds, 10 test episodes, proper confidence intervals, multiple algorithms (PPO, SAC, DPC, TD-MPC), 25k+ GPU hours
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameter documentation, hardware specifications, released code/data/models, pre-computed initial domains, grid refinement validation studies
Clear presentation with well-organized narrative, informative figures, and extensive supplementary materials covering implementation details
Standardized evaluation protocols and train/val/test splits provide useful foundation for future comparisons in AFC community
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Primarily engineering contribution integrating existing components (PICT from Franz et al. 2026) with no new algorithms, theory, or algorithmic insights from experiments

Differentiability claim unsubstantiated: DPC evaluated on only 2/13 environments with training failures (degradation on RBC2D variants, early stopping on CylinderJet2D-easy-v0); limited evaluation undermines a headline contribution

Experimental findings unsurprising: SAC > PPO (expected from literature), transfer learning works (predictable), no algorithmic insights emerge; DPC underperformance unexplained despite direct relevance to differentiability claims

Critical missing comparison with HydroGym (Lagemann et al., 2025b): No direct experimental comparison despite overlap; claims about solver dependencies and differentiability advantages lack empirical validation
MARL support underexplored: Only qualitative observations of coordinated behavior; no systematic quantitative analysis of MARL vs. SARL performance or scalability with agent count

Design choices lack justification: Arbitrary difficulty progression (varying Re alone), hand-crafted reward functions without ablation, observation design not optimized, hyperparameter selection acknowledged as suboptimal

Methodological limitations inadequately addressed: Only 5 random seeds for statistical robustness; baseline quality deviates 3.84% from prior work (Rabault et al.); no systematic hyperparameter sensitivity analysis

Narrow scope and impact: AFC is specialized subdomain; unlike general RL benchmarks, limited applicability across RL community; no evidence benchmark will change research practices vs. existing accessible tools

strengths: Addresses genuine gap in RL for AFC: First benchmark combining no external solver dependencies, full differentiability, native MARL support, and high-fidelity 3D capabilities. Well-motivated by fragmentation in prior work.

Rigorous experimental validation: Solver benchmarked against multiple works (3.84% deviation on cylinder drag), grid refinement studies, proper statistical methodology (5 seeds, 95% confidence intervals via stratified bootstrap, consistent train/val/test protocol).

Comprehensive evaluation at massive scale: 25k+ GPU hours covering PPO, SAC, DPC, TD-MPC across 13 environments with three difficulty levels, transfer learning studies (2D→3D, domain size), and runtime analysis.

Exceptional reproducibility: Complete hyperparameters (Tables 5-7), hardware/software specs, numerical setups with grid refinement, trained models and datasets publicly available. Sets high bar for benchmark paper reproducibility.

Sound technical design: Modular FluidEnv abstraction supporting three interaction modes (SARL/MARL/gradient-based), seamless integration with standard RL libraries (Gymnasium, Stable-Baselines3), GPU parallelization. Proves PyTorch-only approach viable.

Actionable empirical insights: Demonstrates SAC consistently outperforms PPO (except TCF), robust 2D→3D transfer for cylinder flow, emergent multi-agent coordination in RBC3D, DPC 1-2 orders magnitude speedup on easy tasks.
weaknesses: Limited DPC evaluation undermines differentiability claim: Training degradation after 10k steps on CylinderJet2D-easy-v0, evaluation on only 2/13 environments, no systematic investigation of instability causes. Differentiability advantage not thoroughly demonstrated beyond speedup on one easy task.

Reduced statistical robustness from limited random seeds: Authors acknowledge limited seeds due to computational cost. While 5 seeds is reasonable and acknowledged, algorithm comparisons show overlapping confidence intervals (Figures 27-35). Hard 3D Airfoil results use only MA-PPO.

Standard hyperparameters may not reflect optimal performance: Using off-the-shelf hyperparameters for 'comparability' but no ablation on sensitivity or tuning explored. Could misrepresent true algorithmic capabilities.

Scope limited to incompressible flows: No compressible, multiphase, or thermochemical flows. Idealized simulation-only environments lack uncertainties, actuator constraints, sensor noise. No real physical validation of policies.
GPU-only requirement limits accessibility: Custom CUDA kernels required; CPU-only execution unsupported. Section 5 acknowledges this limits accessibility for researchers without GPU resources.

Incomplete algorithmic coverage: Missing recent model-based methods (Dreamer, etc.), only one per algorithm class, limited model-free diversity. TD-MPC and DPC evaluated on subset of environments. No comparison to classical optimal control or evolutionary strategies.
